story.title: Zelenskyy Criticizes Trump's 'Friend' Remark About Putin, Urges US Pressure
story.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed frustration over the U.S. approach to Russia, particularly criticizing Donald Trump's comment referring to Vladimir Putin as 'my friend.' Zelenskyy likened this remark to calling Adolf Hitler a friend during World War II, emphasizing that Putin is an aggressor and should not be viewed as a friend. His comments come amid ongoing tensions related to military support and financial aid for Ukraine.

explore_lenses.label: Why does Zelenskyy reject a neutral U.S. posture?
explore_lenses.title: Kyiv sees engagement without pressure as enabling Russia
explore_lenses.summary: Zelenskyy’s criticism is directed at the perceived balance of U.S. diplomacy, not simply at Trump’s wording. Kyiv argues that treating Moscow and Kyiv symmetrically overlooks Russia’s role as the invading party, while Trump says his personal engagement is intended to secure a deal.

claims.text: Zelenskyy told the BBC that the United States should use its power and standing to pressure Russia; he said neutrality toward an aggressor risks supporting both the victim and the aggressor.
Trump defended calling Putin a friend by saying his objective was to stop the killing and make a deal, rather than to signal approval of Putin’s conduct.

The ICC has issued an arrest warrant for Putin, finding reasonable grounds to believe he bears responsibility for the alleged war crimes of unlawful deportation and transfer of Ukrainian children from occupied areas to Russia; the warrant does not determine guilt at trial.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Zelenskyy’s remarks insulted Putin and showed that Zelenskyy was unwilling to pursue a peace settlement.

explore_lenses.title: European funding is moving, but 2027 backing is unresolved
explore_lenses.summary: A substantial EU payment has been authorized, while leaders were still debating Ukraine’s financing needs for 2027. The reporting also describes U.S.-led peace efforts, but it does not identify a signed agreement or confirmed breakthrough.

claims.text: On November 16, the EU Council approved a payment of just under €8 billion for Ukraine under the Ukraine Facility, including about €5 billion from the Ukraine Support Loan.
The EU Council said the Ukraine Facility has more than €50 billion available through 2027, with regular disbursements linked to Ukraine meeting reform targets in its Ukraine Plan.

European Council President António Costa convened the November 26-27 special meeting specifically to discuss Ukraine financing for 2027 and beyond, with the stated goal of reaching a timely agreement.
According to the Associated Press reporting, EU leaders had not reached consensus on a proposed $49 billion loan for Ukraine’s 2027 economic and military needs.

story_report.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticized Donald Trump’s description of Vladimir Putin as “my friend,” arguing that treating Russia’s leader as a friend was akin to doing so with Adolf Hitler during World War II. Zelenskyy urged Washington to use its power and standing to pressure Russia, saying neutrality toward an aggressor can blur the distinction between victim and attacker. The remarks drew a Kremlin rebuke, with spokesperson Dmitry Peskov calling them insulting to Putin and evidence that Zelenskyy did not want a peace settlement.

sections.heading: Trump and Zelenskyy Differ on Putin
sections.body: Zelenskyy’s criticism reflects a broader dispute over how the United States should engage Moscow while Russia’s war against Ukraine continues. Trump defended his use of the word “friend,” saying his aim was to stop the killing and secure a deal rather than endorse Putin’s conduct. Zelenskyy, by contrast, said U.S. neutrality toward an aggressor risked placing the victim and aggressor on the same footing.

sections.heading: ICC Warrant Shapes Putin Context
sections.body: The International Criminal Court has issued an arrest warrant for Putin, saying there are reasonable grounds to believe he bears responsibility for alleged war crimes involving the unlawful deportation and transfer of Ukrainian children from occupied areas to Russia. The warrant is not a finding of guilt at trial, but it provides legal context for Zelenskyy’s insistence that Putin should be treated as an aggressor rather than a partner.

sections.heading: European Union Financing Remains Unsettled
sections.body: European support remains a central practical issue for Ukraine. On November 16, the EU Council approved a payment of just under €8 billion under the Ukraine Facility, including about €5 billion from the Ukraine Support Loan; the facility has more than €50 billion available through 2027, tied to reform targets in Ukraine’s plan. But EU leaders had not reached consensus on a proposed $49 billion loan for Ukraine’s 2027 economic and military needs, prompting a special European Council meeting on November 26-27 focused on financing beyond 2027.

unresolved.text: Public reporting does not establish whether the U.S. approach will create leverage over Moscow or produce movement toward a settlement, and the cited sources do not confirm a final EU agreement on the proposed 2027 loan.

related_stories.title: Uganda Plans Troop Withdrawal from DR Congo Amid Diplomatic Tensions
related_stories.summary: Uganda's army has announced plans to withdraw its troops from a key town in eastern DR Congo, citing increased attacks from militias reportedly aligned with the Congolese government. This decision comes amid ongoing diplomatic tensions between the two nations, as Uganda has been assisting the Congolese military in combating Islamist militants in the region.

related_stories.title: Iran Rejects Claims of Involvement in Kuwait Strike That Killed Two Italians
related_stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has denied allegations of the country's involvement in a drone strike in Kuwait that resulted in the deaths of two Italian nationals. He described the accusations as baseless and labeled the incident as 'suspicious,' offering to cooperate on a joint investigation. In response, Kuwait condemned the strike as 'heinous Iranian aggression,' with additional condemnations from Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar, and the UAE.
